Both declared checkers exit 0 on the first pass; check-outputs ok.
confidence_rationale: Step 10 HIGH row: the emitted element (Tier2_Escalation__e objectPermissions with allowCreate/allowRead true) traces directly to two sources in the Step 3 inventory - the platform-events-apex skill's gotcha naming Create as the API-67.0 user-mode requirement, and the permission-set-architecture checker's own dependency-chain rule requiring allowRead alongside allowCreate, which is why allowRead is written and not merely assumed. Both cited checkers exited 0 on the first pass, check-outputs returned ok, every declared output was written and nothing else (no new file, no new package.xml member), and the persona question (which permission set the grant belongs in) was answered from the plan's own decision D14 and D10 rather than defaulted or guessed.

process_observations.observation: The fix stayed inside the file the finding named: no new permission set, no new package.xml member, no change to M1-S05's build-level manifest. check_permission_set_architecture.py's dependency-chain rule (allowCreate/allowEdit require allowRead) caught what a build-time read of the platform-events-apex gotcha alone would not have flagged as mandatory - it only names Create - which is why allowRead is written on this row and not just allowCreate.

A future reader should not assume the platform-events skill documents a Create+Read pairing - it documents Create only.

decision_record.question: Which permission set should grant Create/Read on Tier2_Escalation__e to the persona that publishes it (S2-F-13)?
decision_record.answer: The existing Tier2_Webhook_Admin set, not a new set. New objectPermissions row: allowCreate true, allowRead true, allowEdit/allowDelete/viewAllRecords/modifyAllRecords false.
decision_record.source: Upstream artefacts / plan decisions (Step 4 priority 3) - decision D14 (traceability.md, PLAN.md Decisions table) already assigns Tier2_Webhook_Admin to every user who can escalate a Case to Tier_2_Engineering; decision D10 places the EventBus.publish call in that same user's escalating transaction, in Tier2EscalationService, before the Queueable runs. The publishing persona and D14's existing assignee set are the same population.

decision_record.question: Does the new objectPermissions row need allowRead as well as allowCreate?
decision_record.source: Cited skill's checker (Step 3 inventory) - skills/admin/permission-set-architecture/scripts/check_permission_set_architecture.py raises ERROR 'allowCreate/allowEdit require allowRead' when allowCreate is true and allowRead is not. skills/apex/platform-events-apex/references/gotchas.md names only Create as the API-67.0 requirement; Read is not independently required by that skill and is written solely to satisfy the checker's dependency chain.

decision_record.question: Do allowEdit, allowDelete, viewAllRecords or modifyAllRecords apply to the new row?
decision_record.answer: No - all four written false, explicitly, matching this file's existing convention of always writing all six flags.
decision_record.source: The requirement / no answer - a platform event is an immutable stream entry (skills/apex/platform-events-apex/references/gotchas.md, "Treating the __e Object Like a Table"): there is no update or delete DML against a published event, and no clarification or decision asks for view-all/modify-all on this object.
